requirements.requirement: Record every command run through sudo on node1, including the invoking user and timestamp, in /var/log/sudo-commands.log.
requirements.summary: A global sudoers policy directs sudo logging to the required file and enables four-digit years. Validated records show timestamps, invoking user, target user, working directory, and command both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command-log entries out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: The policy disables sudo syslog output, and uniquely marked sudo invocations were absent from both /var/log/messages and /var/log/secure before and after restart.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also strong: it shows a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and bounded disconnection, a changed boot identity, restored system state, active rsyslog, valid persistent configuration, preserved prior log data, and successful new sudo logging. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently confirm the restart.
limitations: Runtime command logging was exercised only with root as the invoking user because no regular login users existed. The global Defaults policy nevertheless applies system-wide, and the resulting record directly demonstrates the required user and timestamp fields.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the sudoers policy was the required implementation; test sudo invocations created bounded verification records; and the scheduled reboot supported the mandatory restart protocol. The temporary sudoers file was atomically moved into its final required location. No failed services, package damage, new exposure, or abandoned temporary residue was observed after execution.
